function: Uplink near-field XL-MIMO channel estimation: a network predicts user angle and distance from camera images to shrink the polar-domain dictionary used by OMP (pp. 2-3).
system: XL-MIMO base station with a 512-element ULA, hybrid analog combining, single-antenna users, near-field, 60 GHz, no RIS (pp. 2, 8).
method: CNN, channel and spatial attention, stacked LSTM trained with MSE loss for angle classification and distance regression (supervised, pp. 3-4, 8); classical OMP recovers the channel (p. 7).
data_channel: DeepSense 6G Scenario 36 (measured images and GPS, 100,000 samples, day and night, p. 7); channel is the analytic near-field spherical-wave model of Eq. (4), pp. 2-3.
test_conditions: Same Scenario 36 data for training and testing, split not described (p. 8); MSE swept over pilot length 20-210 and dictionary offsets at pilot length 120 (p. 9).
baselines: Classical: OMP with full polar-domain dictionary (p. 9). Learned: CNN, ResNet-18, ResNet-34, LSTM on prediction loss (Figs. 6-7, p. 8); own variants ISACE, ISACE-Attention, Pilot-free.
metrics: Channel estimation MSE versus pilot length and dictionary offsets (p. 9); training and test loss per epoch (p. 8); claimed complexity reduction of up to 90% (p. 1).
complexity: None; only a claim of up to 90% lower complexity than full-dictionary OMP (pp. 1-2), with no operation count, parameter count or runtime (pp. 3, 8).
openness: none (no code or data link; DeepSense 6G Scenario 36 is named without a link, p. 7).
q1_support: p. 7: "The dataset used in this paper is the Scenario36 dataset from Deep Sense 6G" (real-world measured images and GPS; the channel itself is analytic, see notes).
q2_support: p. 9: "different methods when the pilot length varies". Only an OMP-stage sweep, since the network input is images only (p. 3: "we utilize image information to predict the distance and angle"); no new scenario, site, band or array size is tested, and the split is not described.
q3_support: p. 9: "The first method involves directly using the OMP algorithm" (non-learned, channel MSE, Fig. 10); p. 8: "our designed HyperDimScaleFusionNet achieves the best performance with a fast convergence rate" (Fig. 7 legend: CNN, Resnet-18, Resnet-34, LSTM, on test loss).
q4_support: p. 1: "reduces the computational complexity of channel estimation by up to 90% compared with conventional methods". Relative claim only: no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime; Tables I-II list layer sizes (p. 3), Tables III-V hyperparameters (p. 8).
q5_support: p. 7: "The dataset used in this paper is the Scenario36 dataset from Deep Sense 6G" (public DeepSense 6G data, named in the criterion); the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included in area 2: the learned network only predicts angle and distance from images to build a smaller polar-domain dictionary, OMP then recovers the near-field channel, and the metric is channel estimation MSE (pp. 2-3, 9), so this is channel estimation and not localization alone. Flags for the reviewer. q1 and q5: only the camera images and GPS of DeepSense 6G Scenario 36 are measured (p. 7); the channel vector is the analytic spherical-wave model of Eq. (4) (p. 3) and the angle labels are not described. q3: the learned baselines CNN, ResNet-18, ResNet-34 and LSTM appear only in Figs. 6-7 (p. 8) as loss versus epoch, with final plateaus that differ by orders of magnitude, not on channel MSE; ISACE, ISACE-Attention and Pilot-free are variants of the proposed network. The text on p. 9 says results are compared against "three other state-of-the-art methods", but Figs. 8-10 show only OMP, Pilot-free and Vision-assisted. q4: only the 90% claim, no cost figure; borderline. PDF check: the first page holds the title 'Vision-Assisted Near-Field Channel Estimation for XL-MIMO Systems' and DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3605377, which match the DOI of the work.
